topic: Planned second FSRU (capacity expansion) and Egypt seasonal vessel-sharing
wiki_text: In February 2026 BOTAŞ announced plans to add a second FSRU at the Dörtyol site, aiming to roughly double the terminal's pipeline send-out capacity from 28 to 56 million cubic meters/day; engineering work is reported ongoing with no FID, vessel, or construction start confirmed as of this batch (July 2026). Separately, under a May 2025 agreement, BOTAŞ has seasonally redeployed the site's FSRU, Ertuğrul Gazi, to Egypt's Ain Sokhna terminal during summer months (when Turkish demand is lower and Egypt's is higher), returning it to Dörtyol off-season.

topic: FSRU vessel history: Vasant 1 to Saros, BOTAŞ's $399M purchase from Swan Energy
wiki_text: The FSRU now stationed at Saros, IMO 9837066, was built in 2020 by Hyundai Heavy Industries as 'Vasant 1' for India's Swan Energy, originally intended for Swan's stalled 5 mtpa Jafrabad LNG import project in Gujarat (delayed repeatedly, including cyclone damage). The vessel was leased to BOTAŞ from around February 2023 and stationed at the Gulf of Saros site. In August 2024, Swan Energy announced it would sell the vessel outright to BOTAŞ Trading for $399 million (paid in tranches), divesting via its subsidiary Triumph Offshore (TOPL), in which Swan held a 51% stake. The vessel's AIS registry name has since been updated to 'Saros', matching the terminal site name; GIIGNL's 2026 report records it as 'Saros (ex Vasant 1)'.

topic: Ownership structure (Kalyon/Kolin/Önal Kardeşler) and vessel replacement history
wiki_text: Etki Liman İşletmeleri Doğalgaz İthalat ve Ticaret AŞ, the terminal-operating company, is owned 50% by Kalyon Group, 30% by Kolin Group, and 20% by the Önal family ('Önal Kardeşler'/Önal Brothers) -- explicitly stated in Turkish trade press covering the delivery of the FSRU vessel. Turkey's first FSRU began service at this Aliağa site in December 2016 using the chartered vessel GDF Suez Neptune (IMO 9385673, from Norway's Höegh LNG). It was replaced in 2019 by a newly built, Kalyon/Kolin-ordered FSRU, 'Turquoise P' (built by Hyundai Heavy Industries, ordered Feb 2017 for ~$230 million, delivered/arrived mid-2019), owned by Pardus Energy and chartered to Etki Liman -- matching GEM's current FloatingVesselName ('FSRU Turquoise').

topic: Fourth storage tank expansion (255,000 to 415,000 cbm), not a regasification-capacity change
wiki_text: On 13 July 2026, BOTAŞ began construction of a fourth LNG storage tank (160,000 cbm) at the Marmara Ereğlisi terminal, per Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, raising total on-site LNG storage capacity from 255,000 to 415,000 cubic meters (a ~60% increase). This is a storage-volume/flexibility investment, distinct from the terminal's regasification throughput -- GIIGNL's nameplate Capacity figure for the site (8.8 MTPA) is unaffected. Daily Sabah separately cites the site's daily regasification capacity as 37 million cubic meters (roughly 9.9-10 MTPA on a simple conversion) -- see companion qa note on this discrepancy.

topic: Black Sea (Sakarya field) LNG-export regulatory enabler -- no named project yet
wiki_text: In October 2025, Turkey amended its Natural Gas Market Law to enable liquefaction and export of gas from its Black Sea Sakarya field, a legal/regulatory milestone. As of this batch (July 2026), no specific liquefaction terminal, FLNG vessel, sponsor, or site has been named -- the change is purely enabling legislation. Routed to the monitor list; does not meet the Discovery add-bar (sponsor + approximate location + concrete step) yet.
